 Judgment:

1. The present complaint is filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954
(herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused have violated the provisions of the

PFA Act and Rules.
2. As per the complaint, on 27-12-2006 at about 6.00 PM Food Inspector Sh. Baljit Singh purchased a sample of "Tomato Ketchup" (3x1200 gms) a food article for analysis from Sh. Amit Kumar of M/s Barista Coffee Company Limited, (A unit of Barista Coffee Company Limited) Store code 001011, 18,
Community Centre New Friends Colony(New), New Delhi where the said food article was being served alongwith sandwiches for sale for human consumption and where the accused No.1 Amit Kumar was found conducting the business of the said food article at the time of sampling.
The sample consisted of 3 sealed packets each containing 100 sachets of 12 gms each and the packets having identical label declaration reproduced by the food inspector on Form VI.

The sample was Da vs Amit Kumar Etc. on 10 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192810032/
3 taken under the supervision/direction of Sh. Sanjay Kaushik.
SDM/LHA.

The sample of "Tomato Ketchup"
was divided equally in three parts so that each one packet constituted one counter part of the sample.

Each sealed packet containing the sample was separately packed,
fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules.
The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample packet.

Notice in Form VI was given to accused No. 1 Amit Kumar and the price of sample was also offered to him vide vendor receipt dated 27-12-2006 but vendor did not accept the same DA vs Amit Kumar etc. stating in writing on vendor's receipt that "We do not sale Tomato Ketchup packet as such.
We serve it to consumer alongwith sandwich including the price of Tomato Ketchup for sale of sandwich.
So the price of Tomato Ketchup not accepted."

Notice in form VI for Barista Coffee Company Limited E-5/B-1, Mohan Cooperative Industrial Area, Mathura Road, New Delhi was also prepared from where the said Tomato Ketchup was supplied to the above said M/s Barista Expresso Bar.
Panchnama too was prepared at the spot.
All the documents prepared by FI were signed by accused Amit Kumar and the other witness Sh Shivjee Mehto, FA.
Before starting sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward, as such Sh. Shivjee Mehto, FA was joined as witness.

3. One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA Code Number 71/LHA/17139 in intact condition alongwith copy of memo in Form VII and another copy of memo in Form VII under seal cover were sent separately to the Public Analyst, Delhi on 28.12.06 and two counterparts of the sample alongwith two copies of memos in Form VII were deposited with the SDM/LHA in intact conditions on 28.12.06.
All copies of Memos in Form VII bear the seal impression with which sample parts were sealed.
Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the sample to be misbranded.

The report of Public Analyst is as follow :-
"The sample is misbranded because there is violation of Rule36(2)(a).

However,
Tomato Ketchup conforms to standard.

The Public Analyst has also reported in the said report regarding label - Complies with Rule 32 but size of label is only 17.58% of the size of packet."
DA vs Amit Kumar etc.
4.

It is the case of the complainant that accused No. 1 Amit Kumar was the vendor-cum-Brew Master of M/s Barista Expresso Bar, (A unit of Barista Coffee Company Limited) Store code 001011, 18,
Community Centre, New Friends Colony(New), New Delhi at the time of taking sample and as such he is incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said unit of the company.

The sampled article of food "Tomato Ketchup"
was supplied by accused No.6 M/s Barista Coffee Company Limited from its Delhi warehouse at E-5/B-1, Mohan Cooperative Industrial Area, Mathura Road, New Delhi.

A number of letters dated 13-3-07, 18-10-07, 2-4-09 and 20-10-09 were Da vs Amit Kumar Etc. on 10 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192810032/
4 sent/delivered by hand to accused No.6 M/s Barista Coffee Company Limited and its various representatives like MD/Company Secretary etc. asking for names of the directors/persons incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the company
but the company deliberately avoided to give the required information.

Accused No.6 M/s Barista Coffee Company Limited has not appointed any nominee both for its vending unit at Store code 001011, 18,Community Centre,
New Friends Colony(New), New Delhi as well as for its warehouse at E-5/B-1, Mohan Cooperative Industrial Area, Mathura Road, New Delhi.

M/s Barista Coffee Company Limited is a company having registered office at Unit No. 2, 4th Floor, D-2, Southern Park, Saket, New Delhi, and it has 4 Directors i.e accused No. 2 Coimbatore Ramanathan Sitaraman, accused No.3 V. Srinivasan, accused No.4 T.V. Vasudev and accused No.5 Partha Dattagupta and as such all the four Directors are incharge of and responsible for day to day DA vs Amit Kumar etc. conduct of the business of the vending unit as well as warehouse of the company.
Being a company M/s Barista Coffee Company Limited is also liable both for the vending unit and its warehouse.

5. It is further stated that the sampled article of food "Tomato Ketchup" was manufactured by M/s Mrs. Beetor's Food Specialities Limited Theing Road, Phillaur,
Distt. Jalandhar- 144410, Punjab and supplied to accused No.6 M/s Barista Coffee Company Limited.
Accused No.8

M / s Mrs.Beetor's Food Specialities Limited is a company and it has appointed accused No. 7 Ram Narain Singh as its nominee under the provisions of PFA Act Rules for its above said works and as such he is incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said unit of the company.
Being a company M/s Mrs. Bector's Food Specialities Limited is also liable.
6. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA.

The complaint was then filed in the court on 19.11.2009 alleging violation of Section 2(ix)&(k) of the PFA Act, 1954, and the provision of Rule 36(2)(a) of PFA Rules 1955, as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act by the accused person.
7. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 23.08.2010.

Based on the report of the PA, notice under section 251 Cr.PC was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ix) & (k) of the DA vs Amit Kumar etc. PFA Act, 1954 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

He also sent letters Ex.PW-2/H to M/s Bectors Food Specialties Ltd., Theing Road, Phillaur, Jalandhar, Punjab and received its reply Ex.PW-2/I alongwith a copy of Form VAT-IV Mark-2/1, the copy of nomination which was in the name of the accused Ram Narayan Singh vide Ex. Mark 2/2 and the Memorandum and Articles of Association of M/s Mrs. Bector's Food Specialties Ltd. Ex.PW-2/K (colly.).

As per reply Ex.PW-2/I, the Managing Director Sh. Akshay Bector admitted and confirmed the supply of sample commodity i.e. Tomato Ketchup vide invoice no. 4423 dated 24.11.2006 to M/s Barista Expresso Bar

After completion of investigation, PW-2 FI Virender Singh submitted the report to LHA/SDM Sh. Lallan Singh for grant of sanction of Director PFA and received the consent/sanction order Ex. PW-2/ of Sh. D.P.Dwivedi, the then Director PFA Department through LHA/SDM.
Thereafter the present complaint DA vs Amit Kumar etc.
Ex . PW-2
/ M was filed in the Court.

Then, Intimation letter Ex. PW- 2/N (OSR) alongwith copies of PA's Report were sent through SDM/LHA Ms. Juhi Mukherjee to the accused persons through registered post Ex. PW2/O which were not received back undelivered.
All the witnesses were duly cross examined by the Ld Defence Counsel.
9. Statement of the accused No. 7 under section 313 CrPC was recorded on 18.01.2018 wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence.
The accused has not led any defence evidence in this case.
10. I have heard Ld. SPP for state and Ld. Counsel for accused.
11. In a criminal trial, the burden is on the complainant / prosecution to establish its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
This burden cannot be shifted to the accused and has to be necessarily discharged by the prosecution itself by leading cogent and trustworthy evidence.
However, if the accused has any defence, then the burden to prove that defence lies upon the accused.
12. The present case is for misbranding of a food article.

As per prosecution the sample was misbranded because there was a violation of Rule 36(2)(a) of PFA Rules,
which provides certain size of label.
13. Regarding the allegations of misbranding, the defence has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in S.S. Gokul DA vs Amit Kumar etc.

entities.text: S.S. Gokul DA vs Amit Kumar etc
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Krishanan & Others vs State 2009(1) FAC 132 to argue that there was a policy of the complainant department of 1985 numbered as Policy No F6(228)/85/ENF/PFA wherein a decision was taken to give a written warning to the offenders with regard to any deficiency in respect of Rule 32 of the PFA Act.

Although this policy was withdrawn by order No. 5/07 dated 14.09.2007 but since in this case the sample was Da vs Amit Kumar Etc. on 10 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192810032/
7 lifted on 27/12/2006, the accused are covered by aforesaid policy.

Although, no such policy has been placed or proved on record by other side and this policy was further withdrawn as per the aforesaid judgment on the ground that Section 20 of the PFA Act does not confer any such power on the consenting authority to issue such warning to the vendors found committing the offence of misbranding.

14. Be that as it may, PFA Act or Rules does not provide any such warning but since the benefit of this policy has been given in the case of S.S. Gokul Krishnan (referred above), I feel myself bound by the ratio of that case.

Therefore as far as offence of misbranding is concerned, since, it is not the case of the prosecution that the accused were given earlier a warning and despite that they continued with the offence, the accused are given the benefit of this policy and therefore they shall not be liable for violation of Rule 36 of PFA Rules.

The judgment of Gokul Krishnan (supra) has also been followed in the judgment of M/s Bunge India Pvt Ltd & Others vs State &
Another Crl.MC 439/2008 dated 20.01.2011 and recently in in Hello Minerals Water PVT LTD & Ors vs State CRL.MC.224/2016 dated 10.01.2018.
